tasks.title: Initialize project with Vite, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind, and dependencies
tasks.description: Set up the Vite project with React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS v4, and install all required libraries: Zustand, @dnd-kit, lucide-react, clsx, tailwind-merge, Vitest.
tasks.details: Run `npm create vite@latest flowline-mvp -- --template react-ts` to scaffold the project. Upgrade React to v19 and ensure TypeScript is in strict mode (set `"strict": true` in tsconfig.json). Install Tailwind CSS v4 following its Vite plugin instructions: `npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite` and add the plugin to `vite.config.ts`. Install Zustand: `npm install zustand`; @dnd-kit: `npm install @dnd-kit/core @dnd-kit/sortable @dnd-kit/utilities`; lucide-react: `npm install lucide-react`; clsx and tailwind-merge: `npm install clsx tailwind-merge`. Install Vitest as dev dependency: `npm install -D vitest`. Configure `package.json` scripts: `"dev": "vite"`, `"build": "tsc && vite build"`, `"test": "vitest"`. Create a basic Tailwind entry CSS file and import it in `main.tsx`. Verify that `npm run dev` starts without errors.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run dev` to ensure the development server starts. Run `npm run build` to confirm TypeScript compilation and production build succeed. Run `npm test` to check Vitest runs (even with no tests yet). Confirm all dependencies are listed in package.json.

tasks.title: Define domain model types and constants
tasks.description: Create TypeScript interfaces, enums, and constants for Scope, Item, Edge, LimitPolicy, Objective, KeyResult, plus resolution, item type, state, dependency kinds, and lifecycle columns.
tasks.details: In a new file `src/types.ts`, define: `Resolution = 'L1' | 'L2' | 'L3'`; `ItemType = 'initiative' | 'epic' | 'story' | 'defect'`; `State` union for all lifecycle states: `'Idea' | 'Option' | 'Bet' | 'Committed' | 'Rejected' | 'Dormant' | 'Backlog' | 'Analyze' | 'In Progress' | 'Ready' | 'Done' | 'Review'`. Interface `Scope` with `id: string; name: string; kind: 'enterprise' | 'value_stream' | 'team' | 'function'; parentId?: string`. Interface `Item` with `id, title, description?, type, valueStreamId, teamId?, state, size?, assignee?, createdAt, resolvedAt?`. Interface `DependencyInfo` with `fsKind: 'FS' | 'SS' | 'FF'`, `lagDays?`, `status: 'proposed' | 'confirmed' | 'rejected'`, `reason?`. Interface `Edge` with `id, kind: 'decomposition' | 'dependency' | 'attribution', from: string, to: string, dep?: DependencyInfo`. Interface `LimitPolicy` with `id, resolution, itemType, scopeId?, column?, enforcement: 'soft' | 'hard', thresholds: { yellow: number, red: number }`. Interface `Objective` and `KeyResult` for commitment-limited entities: Objective with `id, name, description?` and KeyResult with `id, objectiveId, description, target, current`. Define column mappings: `COLUMNS_BY_RESOLUTION: Record<Resolution, State[]>` mapping L1 to `['Idea', 'Option', 'Bet', 'Committed', 'Rejected', 'Dormant']`, L2 to `['Backlog', 'Analyze', 'In Progress', 'Ready', 'Done']`, L3 to `['Backlog', 'In Progress', 'Review', 'Done']` (adjust defect lifecycle to same states). Export all types and constants.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run build` to ensure TypeScript compiles without errors. Add basic type-level tests if desired (e.g., using `tsd` or simply rely on build). Ensure no `board` field exists on Item.

tasks.title: Implement seed data and Zustand store with localStorage persistence
tasks.description: Create a seeded in-memory demo enterprise graph and set up a Zustand store with actions to update items, edges, and reset to seed.
tasks.details: In `src/seed.ts`, construct the demo enterprise exactly as described: one enterprise scope 'Acme', two value streams 'Core Experience' and 'Platform Services', three teams: Team Alpha, Team Bravo (under Core Experience), Team Platform (under Platform Services). Create one initiative 'Onboarding Redesign' decomposing into 5 epics across both streams (e.g., 3 in Core Experience, 2 in Platform Services). Ensure one epic (e.g., 'API decision') is in Platform Services and is a blocker for a story in Team Bravo. Create 2 objectives and several stories attributed many-to-many; ensure one story is attributed to both objectives. Create stories under each epic, including ~18 open descendants in one epic to show composition pressure. Include a defect. Set limit policy: epic per value stream limit = 4, seeded with 5 epics in one stream to demonstrate soft block. Use a separate `edges` array with instances for decomposition, dependency, and attribution edges. In `src/store.ts`, define a Zustand store with state: `items: Item[]`, `scopes: Scope[]`, `edges: Edge[]`, `objectives: Objective[]`, `keyResults: KeyResult[]`, `limitPolicies: LimitPolicy[]`, `resolution: Resolution`, `selectedScopeId: string | null`, and actions: `updateItem(id, patch)`, `addEdge(edge)`, `updateEdge(id, patch)`, `resetDemo()`, `setResolution(r)`, `setSelectedScope(id)`. Use Zustand `persist` middleware with name 'flowline-mvp' to persist to localStorage. On first load, use seed data. Provide `resetDemo` to restore seed and clear persisted state.
tasks.testStrategy: Write Vitest tests to verify seed data integrity: number of items, edges, correct level relationships, limit policy, etc. Test store initialization and hydration from localStorage (simulate by setting localStorage). Test `resetDemo` restores original seed.

tasks.title: Implement derivation functions: level, dependencyState, portfolioStatus, and WIP counting
tasks.description: Create pure functions to compute item level, dependency state, portfolio status, and work-in-progress counts excluding attribution edges.
tasks.details: In `src/derivations.ts`, implement: `level(itemId: string, items: Item[], edges: Edge[]): Resolution` following rules: if item.type is initiative → 'L1'; else if item decomposes into epics (i.e., there exists an edge of kind 'decomposition' from item to an item of type 'epic') → 'L2'; else if decomposes into stories/defects → 'L3'; else 'L3' (schedulable floor). `dependencyState(blockerId: string, dependentId: string, items: Item[], edges: Edge[]): string` using rules: dependent resolved → 'Closed'; blocker resolved, dependent unresolved → 'Satisfied'; blocker unresolved, dependent not started → 'Open (planning risk)'; blocker unresolved, dependent in progress → 'Open (live blockage)'; blocker cancelled → 'Void'. Need to determine 'cancelled' state (maybe blocker state is 'Rejected' for initiatives or 'Done' for resolved, 'Dormant' cancelled?). Define a helper to check resolved and cancelled based on item type and state. `portfolioStatus(initiativeId: string, items: Item[], edges: Edge[]): string` computed from committed/decomposed epics: e.g., aggregate states of child epics (e.g., if all Done → 'Done', if any In Progress → 'In Progress', etc.) or a simplified algorithm: count epics in each state and derive. `getWIPCount(scopeId: string, resolution: Resolution, items: Item[], edges: Edge[]): number` returns count of items in scope (via valueStreamId/teamId depending on resolution?) excluding attribution. Specifically, for attribution, edge kind 'attribution' should not cause an item to be counted multiple times; count each item once if it belongs to scope. Implement helper `getBoardItems(scopeId, resolution, items, edges, scopes)` that returns items visible on the board, handling boundary pins and ghost lane. All functions must be pure and typed.
tasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests in Vitest for each function: test level computation for initiative, epic with child epics/stories, story; test dependencyState transitions (resolving blocker flips dependent to Satisfied; rejecting/cancelling blocker gives Void; etc.); test portfolioStatus for combinations of epic states; test WIP counting excludes attribution and counts a story attributed to two objectives as one unit. Ensure no level field is used.

tasks.title: Build board layout components: columns, scope lanes, lane headers, and card containers
tasks.description: Create the main board UI with vertical state columns and horizontal scope lanes, including lane headers with count/limit and row rails.
tasks.details: In `src/components/Board.tsx`, build a grid layout using Tailwind. Columns are determined by the current resolution from `COLUMNS_BY_RESOLUTION`. Lanes are determined by selected scope: if scope is enterprise, lanes are value streams; if scope is value stream, lanes are teams; if scope is team, single lane. Use Zustand store to get scopes, items, edges, limitPolicies. Compute per lane and column the visible items using `getBoardItems` or similar. Render lane headers showing `count / limit` where count is WIP count for that lane and column, limit from LimitPolicy for corresponding item type and scope. Color threshold: yellow when count >= 70% of limit, red when >= limit. Row rail on the left shows per-row total count. Use `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` for class composition. Ensure the layout is dense like LeanKit: small cards, compact spacing.
tasks.testStrategy: Write component tests using React Testing Library (if desired) or manual testing: render Board with seed data, verify columns appear based on resolution, lanes appear, lane headers show correct counts and colors for yellow/red thresholds. Ensure row rail shows correct totals. Check that no items appear twice due to attribution on same lane.

tasks.title: Implement resolution switcher and board data computation
tasks.description: Add top bar resolution switcher (Initiative L1 / Epic L2 / Story L3) and update board columns and counting unit accordingly while preserving scope.
tasks.details: In `src/components/TopBar.tsx` (or within Board), add three buttons for L1/L2/L3. On click, call `setResolution` from store. The board (already dependent on resolution) will re-render with new columns and item mapping. Ensure that switching resolution does not change selected scope. The counting unit: for L1, count initiatives; L2 count epics; L3 count stories/defects. Items that are not of the current resolution but have decomposition to items of that resolution should appear as boundary pins (e.g., epic on L3 board). Implement logic in `getBoardItems` to map items to columns based on level and state. For each item, if its computed level equals resolution, it is a regular card; if level > resolution (e.g., initiative on L2 board), it appears as rollup contribution or not shown? The PRD says: 'One epic renders on three boards with one identity: L2 card on its value-stream board, L3 boundary pin on a team board, rollup contribution on the L1 portfolio.' So for L3 board, an epic (level L2) should appear as a boundary pin in the column corresponding to its state? Actually boundary pin is shown where it does not belong, e.g., epic on team board (L3). So implement: if item's computed level != resolution, but item has descendants of the current resolution, show as boundary pin in the appropriate column (the column of the descendant? or a ghost lane?). The PRD: 'Boundary pins: a card shown where it does not belong renders with no pill, no WIP count, dashed left border, "waiting on: <title>"'. Also 'Ghost lane: when a dependency enters from outside the scope, a read-only lane at the board edge lists only the binding items.' We'll implement boundary pins and ghost lane in later tasks. For now, ensure resolution switcher updates columns and counting unit.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual test: switch between L1, L2, L3 and verify columns change to respective lifecycles and items appear/disappear as appropriate. Check that selected scope remains unchanged. Unit test the mapping function that transforms items to board slots based on resolution.

tasks.title: Implement card component and boundary pin rendering
tasks.description: Create card component with type pill, title, id+size, value stream stripe, icon row, and distinct boundary pin styling.
tasks.details: In `src/components/Card.tsx`, render an item card with: type pill color-coded by type (initiative=purple, epic=blue, story=green, defect=red), title, bottom row showing id and size (e.g., '#123 · 5 pts'), left border stripe colored by value stream (map valueStreamId to color), icon row at bottom showing dependency count (number of dependency edges where item is blocker or dependent), child count (number of decomposition edges from item), and blocked flag if any dependency open. For boundary pins (when item is shown outside its natural level), render without type pill, no WIP count contribution, dashed left border, and text 'waiting on: <title>' where title is the dependent's title (or blocker's title?). The PRD says "waiting on: <title>" and opens the item in a side panel scoped to its own board. Implement conditional rendering based on a prop `isBoundaryPin`. Use lucide-react icons for counts and flags.
tasks.testStrategy: Component test: render a regular card and verify all elements present. Render a boundary pin variant and ensure no pill, dashed border, and 'waiting on' text appears. Verify that the card does not affect WIP count when in boundary pin mode (by checking that the count computation excludes it).

tasks.title: Implement item side panel with details, children, dependencies, and derivation display
tasks.description: Create a side panel that opens when clicking a card, showing the item's full details, its children, dependencies, computed level and dependency states with derivation explanation.
tasks.details: In `src/components/SidePanel.tsx`, use Zustand to get selected item (add `selectedItemId` to store with action `setSelectedItemId`). The panel slides in from right side. Show item title, type, state, value stream, team, size, assignee, createdAt. Show children section: list of child items via decomposition edges, with ability to click to navigate (set selected item). Show dependencies section: list of dependency edges involving this item (both as blocker and dependent), with status and actions to confirm/reject (for proposed) and maybe resolve. Show computed level: display `level(item)` result and the decomposition path used. Show dependency state for each dependency: display `dependencyState(blocker, dependent)` and the reasons. For boundary pins, ensure panel is scoped to the item's own board (meaning the panel shows the item in its natural resolution context, not the current board resolution). Implement by passing the item's computed level to the panel content.
tasks.testStrategy: Test manually: click on a regular card, panel opens with correct details. Click on a boundary pin, panel shows content appropriate to the item's own level (e.g., epic details, not story details). Verify children and dependency lists are accurate. Check that dependency actions (confirm/reject) work and update edge status.

tasks.title: Implement drag-and-drop with dnd-kit for moving cards between columns
tasks.description: Enable drag-and-drop of cards between columns to update item state, triggering level recomputation when children are moved.
tasks.details: In Board component, wrap each card with dnd-kit's `useDraggable` and each column with `useDroppable`. On drag end, determine target column state and call `updateItem(itemId, { state: newState })`. Only allow dragging regular cards (not boundary pins) and only within the current resolution's columns. For L2 resolution, dragging an epic between columns updates its state; moving an epic to a column that reflects decomposition? No, only state changes. For L3, dragging a story updates its story state. After any state change, derived values (level, dependency states, portfolio status) will recompute automatically. To demonstrate level change via decomposition: implement ability to drag child items away from a parent? That might be done via side panel editing children, not drag. The PRD says "Dragging all children away from an epic changes its computed level." This implies moving decomposition edges, possibly via UI to reassign parent. For MVP, we can implement in side panel a 'change parent' action or drag between cards to establish decomposition? Simplify: add a button in side panel to detach child from parent, or drag child card onto another card to set as new parent? The PRD does not specify exactly how; we can implement a simple method: in side panel, for each child, provide a 'Detach' button that removes the decomposition edge, and maybe a 'Reparent' option. That is sufficient to show level change. Ensure that after detach, the epic's level recomputes to L3 if no children left.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test the store update logic: when item state changes, all derived functions reflect changes. Integration test: drag a card to another column, verify state updates. Simulate detaching all children from an epic, verify its computed level changes from L2 to L3.

tasks.title: Implement dependency management and computed dependency state updates
tasks.description: Add UI to create, confirm, reject, and resolve dependencies; ensure dependent state automatically updates when blocker resolves.
tasks.details: In side panel dependencies section, provide a button 'Add dependency' that allows selecting another item and creating a dependency edge with default status 'proposed'. For each dependency, show actions: confirm (set status to 'confirmed'), reject (set status to 'rejected'), and for blocker items, a 'Resolve' button that updates the blocker item's state to its resolved state (e.g., for epic, set state to 'Done'; for story, set to 'Done'). The dependent's dependency state will then recompute to 'Satisfied' automatically (via derivation). Ensure that when a dependency is confirmed, the dependent shows blocked flag if blocker unresolved. Also implement cross-level dependency: the seeded dependency from Platform epic to Team Bravo story should display correctly on both boards, with the epic appearing as boundary pin on the story's board. Use `dependencyState` function to display the current state and reason. Ensure attribution edges are not considered dependencies.
tasks.testStrategy: Test manually: open the blocked story's panel, see the dependency on 'API decision' epic with status. Click 'Resolve' on the blocker epic; verify the story's dependency state changes to 'Satisfied' and the blocked flag disappears. Unit test the update logic for confirming/rejecting dependencies. Verify that resolving blocker updates state on both boards without manual edit.

tasks.title: Implement limit policy enforcement and composition pressure display
tasks.description: Add soft-block enforcement for item limits per scope, requiring a reason before allowing a move that would exceed limit; show composition pressure on cards with many open descendants.
tasks.details: When a drag-and-drop operation would cause a lane's count to exceed its limit (e.g., adding a 5th epic to a value stream with limit 4), intercept the drop and open a dialog (LimitDialog) requiring the user to enter a reason (text input). Only after entering a non-empty reason, allow the move (call updateItem) and record the reason (could store in a separate log or on the item as `limitOverrideReason`). Show a toast or indicator. For composition pressure: on cards that have many open descendants (e.g., epic with 18 open stories), display a visual indicator (e.g., a small pressure icon or red dot) and tooltip with count of open children. This is computed from decomposition edges and child states. No hard block; always soft. Ensure limit policies are configurable but seeded with epic limit per value stream = 4.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual test: attempt to drag a 5th epic into a column that would exceed the limit; dialog appears, cannot proceed without reason. Enter reason, move allowed. Check composition pressure indicator on the seeded epic with many open descendants. Unit test the function that checks limit thresholds and returns whether a move requires reason.

tasks.title: Implement portfolio rollup, reset demo, search, zoom, and final integration
tasks.description: Add a portfolio view with computed initiative status, plus top bar search and zoom controls, and ensure reset demo restores seed.
tasks.details: In the portfolio view, show a list of initiatives with their computed status. Add a 'Reset demo' button in top bar that calls `resetDemo` from store. Add search input in top bar that filters cards by title or id. Add zoom controls (buttons for 75%, 100%, 125%) that scale the board via CSS transform. Ensure all features integrate without errors. Run build and tests.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual test: open the portfolio view, see initiative with computed status. Test reset demo: after making changes, click reset and verify board returns to seed state. Test search filters visible cards. Test zoom changes scale. Run `npm run build` and `npm test` to ensure green.

tasks.title: Implement Objective and Key Result data model and persistence
tasks.description: Define and persist Objectives and Key Results as commitment-limited entities with period, status, score, target, current, and progress fields.
tasks.details: Create types: Objective { id, title, description?, period, status: 'active' | 'scored', score? } and KeyResult { id, objectiveId, title, target?, current?, progress? }. Store in workspace JSON/state using normalized lookup maps. Validate objectiveId exists, period is non-empty, status is valid, and numeric fields are non-negative when present. Ensure these entities are not represented as cards or lanes.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test CRUD roundtrip for both entities. Reject KeyResults with missing or invalid objectiveId. Verify persisted state reloads correctly and no lane or WIP entities are created.

tasks.title: Build Objectives & Key Results view with period selector and score summary
tasks.description: Create the OKR view where objectives are listed by period, with commitment limit status and score summary, and nested key results.
tasks.details: Build an OKR page that filters objectives by period and shows active versus scored state. Display the period commitment limit indicator, defaulting to 3-5 active objectives. Show nested KeyResults below each objective and compute an overall score summary for the selected period.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify each period filter shows the correct objectives. Confirm score summary recalculates after score changes. Confirm commitment-limit highlight appears when active objective count is outside the 3-5 range.

tasks.title: Implement Objective create, edit, delete, and status workflow
tasks.description: Add UI and behavior to create, edit, delete, activate, score, and close Objectives.
tasks.details: Create a form/modal for Objective title, description, period, status, and score. Support active-to-scored transitions. Validate against commitment limits from task 2. Use confirm-before-destructive actions. Persist updates through the Objective store.
tasks.testStrategy: Create an objective and verify it appears in the selected period. Edit fields and confirm persistence. Activate and score an objective. Delete with confirmation and verify dependent KeyResults are handled.

tasks.title: Implement Key Result add, edit, and score UI
tasks.description: Add the ability to create, edit, update current/target values, and score Key Results under Objectives.
tasks.details: Within the OKR view, allow adding/editing KRs for a selected objective. Support target, current, and progress fields. Compute progress from current/target where possible. Score KRs without placing them in board columns or affecting WIP.
tasks.testStrategy: Add KRs under multiple objectives. Edit target/current and confirm progress calculation. Score KRs and verify objective score summary updates. Validate that KRs do not appear in lanes or WIP calculations.

tasks.title: Implement objective-work attribution edges and rollup computation
tasks.description: Implement many-to-many attribution edges from initiatives and cards to objectives, and compute objective rollup without inflating WIP.
tasks.details: Create attribution edge records for many-to-many linkage between work items and objectives. Provide query helpers that return attributed initiatives/cards for an objective. Calculate coverage and rollup status/percent complete from attributed work. Ensure attribution edges never count as WIP.
tasks.testStrategy: Link and unlink work to objectives. Verify no WIP count changes. Verify objective rollup percentage reflects attributed work progress only. Test with multiple initiatives and cards.

tasks.title: Build map-work-to-objectives UI and attribution UX with coverage/impact reporting
tasks.description: Allow attaching initiatives and cards to objectives and display coverage, rollup status, and percent of attributed work.
tasks.details: Add an objective attribution control to initiative/card panels and item editors. Show objective chips on attributed work. Display coverage percentages and unattributed-work hints. Provide impact reporting so users can see how mapped work contributes to an objective.
tasks.testStrategy: Attach/detach initiatives and cards to objectives. Confirm objective coverage updates immediately. Verify the coverage report lists the correct work and excludes unattributed work.

tasks.title: Implement cross-board initiative rollup and board-local top-level initiative semantics
tasks.description: Enable top-level initiatives from one management board to roll up to top-level initiatives on another management board, while preserving board-local top-level definitions.
tasks.details: Define an initiative decomposition tree that spans boards. A top-level initiative on a management board can roll up to a top-level initiative on another management board. On any management board, an initiative whose parent is not on the same board is treated as board-local top-level. Update the Initiatives workflow to reflect these board-local top-level initiatives.
tasks.testStrategy: Create parent/child initiatives across boards. Verify cross-board rollup path. Verify a child with an off-board parent appears as top-level on its local board. Verify management board Initiatives workflow shows only board-local top-level initiatives.

tasks.title: Column WIP limits: board-level enforcement mode with at/over tints
tasks.description: Per-lane WIP limits with a board-level enforcement mode and yellow/red column tints. No thresholds, effective dates, or soft-block.
tasks.details: Keep the per-lane wipLimit. Add Board.wipEnforcement ('visualize' | 'block'; default visualize). A lane whose card count reaches its limit gets an amber tint (header + body); over the limit it gets a red tint. In 'block' mode a move that would push the target lane or any limited ancestor over its limit is rejected; 'visualize' only tints. A board-level WIP selector lives in the board header (edit mode); the WIP limit input is available on leaf lanes including top-level columns. No thresholds, effective dates, or soft-block.
tasks.testStrategy: wipState reports at / over the limit. Set a lane limit and verify amber at the limit and red over it. In 'block' mode a move that would exceed is rejected; in 'visualize' it is allowed. setBoardWipEnforcement persists. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Implement initiative health and at-risk flags beyond percent complete
tasks.description: Add P2 initiative health and at-risk flags based on signals beyond simple percent complete.
tasks.details: Define rules for health flags using blockers, dependency risk, stale progress, uncovered work, and rollup anomalies. Add flag badges in portfolio and initiative views. Keep rule evaluation on compact state/derived selectors.
tasks.testStrategy: Seed initiatives with blockers, stale progress, and uncovered children. Confirm expected at-risk flags appear. Verify flags clear when conditions are resolved.

tasks.title: Build full card editor in side panel
tasks.description: P0 full card editor supports title, markdown description, assignee, size, and type in the side panel.
tasks.details: Create a panel that opens when a card is selected. Include title input, markdown description editor/preview, assignee picker, size field, and issue type selector. Persist all changes immediately or on save/cancel. Integrate with existing item store and undo stack.
tasks.testStrategy: Open editor for a card. Change title, description markdown, assignee, size, and type. Verify each persists and renders correctly. Test save and cancel behavior.

tasks.title: Implement archive items (clear Done work off boards, keep it searchable)
tasks.description: Archive items so completed (Done) work can be cleared off boards without deleting it; archived items leave the boards but stay searchable and still appear in linked-issue surfaces. Deletion is split into a separate task (39).
tasks.details: Add an `archived` flag (with `archivedAt`) to Item and 'archived'/'unarchived' item-log events. Provide archive/unarchive actions: a per-card action, a board-level 'Archive done' bulk action (archive every Done item on a board), and a user-set auto-archive after N days in Done (applied on load and when changed; each archive is logged). Archiving a parent cascades to its whole subtree; unarchive restores it. Archived items are excluded from board rendering (cards workflow, initiatives workflow, boundary pins, lane WIP counts) so they do not clutter, but remain in the data: rollup still counts them and they still appear in linked-issue lists (hierarchy children, links) with an 'archived' marker. Add an Archive view (top bar) listing archived items with search, restore, and the auto-archive setting. Record resolvedAt when an item enters/leaves a Done lane so auto-archive has a clock.
tasks.testStrategy: Archive a leaf and a parent; verify the whole subtree is archived, hidden from the board and its lane counts, yet still listed in the parent's children and the Archive view/search. Unarchive restores the subtree. Bulk 'Archive done' archives all resolved board cards. Auto-archive archives only items whose resolvedAt is older than the threshold. Verify rollup still counts archived leaves and that no archived item appears on a board.

tasks.title: Implement quick-add and paste-many card creation in lanes
tasks.description: P1 quick-add and paste-many: paste a list into a lane to create multiple cards.
tasks.details: Add a lane-level composer with quick-add for a single card and a paste area for multi-line text. Parse lines as separate card titles. Create cards sequentially in the lane. Show feedback and allow undo for the batch.
tasks.testStrategy: Paste a bulleted or line-separated list. Confirm one card is created per non-empty line. Verify cards appear in order in the correct lane. Undo the batch and confirm all created cards are removed.

tasks.title: Add checklists inside a card
tasks.description: P2 checklist support inside a card for finer-grained work than schedulable cards.
tasks.details: Add checklist model data inside items. Provide UI to add, check, uncheck, reorder, and delete checklist entries. Show checklist progress on the card face. Do not treat checklist items as schedulable work or WIP.
tasks.testStrategy: Create checklist items, reorder them, check/uncheck, and verify progress summary on card. Confirm checklist items never appear in lane or WIP counts.

tasks.title: Add comments and activity log per item
tasks.description: P2 comments and activity log per item.
tasks.details: Add a chronological activity log to each item. Support adding comments and automatically record meaningful changes such as title, assignee, status, type, size, dependency changes, and rollup changes. Render markdown in comments.
tasks.testStrategy: Add a comment and confirm it appears. Trigger several item changes and verify the activity log records them in order. Confirm activity log is scoped to the correct item.

tasks.title: Implement multi-select and bulk actions
tasks.description: P2 multi-select cards (shift+click) and bulk actions for move to lane, retype, assign, archive, and delete.
tasks.details: Shift+click a card to start a multi-select group: the first shift+click seeds from the open card, later ones add/remove, and the item panel disappears. A floating bulk-action sub-menu appears while a group is selected: move to lane, change type, assign, archive, delete, clear. Selected cards get an indigo ring. Type changes refuse the reserved Initiative type; a blank assignee unassigns; moving into a Done lane starts the auto-archive clock. Opening a card or switching boards clears the group. Deep link ?select=id1,id2. Moving to another board is deferred (task 42).
tasks.testStrategy: Store tests: shift+click seeds from the open card and toggles; bulk type/assign/move/archive/delete update every selected item; Initiative type is refused; the group clears on open. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Implement lane reorder and add via buttons (Cards workflow)
tasks.description: P0 button-driven board editing for the Cards workflow: move columns left/right and rows up/down, and add a column to a column split or a row to a row split. No drag; order persists.
tasks.details: Scope: the Cards workflow only (the Initiatives workflow is static/derived; management boards are unaffected). Add a moveLane(laneId, delta) action that reorders a lane within its parent and renumbers siblings (0..n-1). Expose ◀ ▶ buttons for column containers and ▲ ▼ for row containers, disabled at the ends. Top-level columns (Backlog / Not Started / In Progress / Done) are fixed in place — only sub-lanes move, and only within their top-level parent. Add '＋ add column' / '＋ add row' buttons on any split container (including top-level splits such as In Progress), labelled by the container's orientation. Keep the existing split / rename / remove / flip / WIP controls. All editing lives in edit mode behind Save/Cancel; lane order is persisted as Lane.order. tasks.title: Add Backlog status and column to standard workflows and seeded boards
tasks.description: Introduce a Backlog stage for initiatives and cards, add Backlog columns to all seeded boards, and enforce hierarchical stage derivation so any Backlog descendant forces its ancestors into Backlog.
tasks.details:
Extend the workflow status enum/type with BACKLOG and order it before the committed statuses (Not Started, In Progress, Done). Treat Backlog as the only uncommitted state. Update the standard workflow definitions for initiatives and cards to include Backlog as the first stage, and update the board/lane column definitions so each seeded board includes a Backlog column/lane mapped to the Backlog status.

Update seed data and any idempotent seed/migration logic so all seeded boards receive the new Backlog column. Preserve existing column ordering by inserting Backlog before Not Started. If columns have WIP limits, Backlog should not impose a committed-work WIP limit.

Implement the hierarchical stage invariant in the domain/service layer, not only in the UI. For an item, treat any childless descendant as a leaf. If the item itself has no children, its own status is its leaf status. The effective stage should be computed as follows: collect all descendant leaves; if any leaf is BACKLOG, return BACKLOG; otherwise derive the committed stage from those leaves using the existing roll-up rules (for example, any In Progress leaf makes the ancestor In Progress; otherwise any Not Started leaf makes it Not Started; otherwise Done).

Add a validation guard when changing an item's status or accepting a move/drop: reject any attempt to place a parent in a committed status while any descendant leaf remains Backlog. When a leaf changes into Backlog, recalculate ancestors so they become Backlog. When the last Backlog descendant moves out of Backlog, recalculate ancestors back to the appropriate committed stage. Ensure recalculation is transactional and covers deep initiative/card hierarchies.

Update API DTOs, serializers, filters, board counts, and any status-transition actions to accept and expose Backlog. Ensure drag-and-drop into the Backlog column updates the card/initiative status and triggers the same roll-up/invariant logic as direct status changes.
tasks.testStrategy:
Write unit tests for the stage derivation function: a parent with one Backlog child resolves to Backlog; an ancestor with a Backlog grandchild resolves to Backlog; a parent whose children are all Done resolves to Done; a parent with mixed Not Started, In Progress, and Done leaves resolves according to the committed roll-up rules; and an item with no children returns its own status.

Add invariant tests proving that attempting to move a parent to Not Started, In Progress, or Done while a descendant leaf is Backlog is rejected. Verify that moving the last Backlog descendant out of Backlog recalculates all affected ancestors to the correct committed stage, and that moving any leaf into Backlog immediately makes all ancestors Backlog.

Add seed/board verification tests asserting that every seeded board includes a Backlog column in the first position and that the standard initiative and card workflows include Backlog before Not Started. Run seed/migration tests to confirm idempotency.

Manually verify that seeded boards render Backlog as the first lane, cards can be dragged into Backlog, the status updates correctly, ancestor lanes reflect Backlog, and dragging the last Backlog child out clears the parent Backlog state. Confirm that no committed parent can be shown with an uncommitted Backlog descendant after moves or direct status changes.

tasks.title: Quarterly planning: plan a department's initiatives across its teams, mapped to OKRs
tasks.description: Support a department running quarterly planning with its teams: each team ends up with a list of initiatives for the quarter, all connected to OKRs.
tasks.details: THE ACTIVITY. A department (a portfolio board plus its linked team boards) sits down with its teams once a quarter and decides which initiatives each team will take on. The outcome to aim for: every team has a list of initiatives for that quarter, and every initiative is connected to at least one OKR. Discovery is part of this task — the exact feature set is not settled, so start with a short design pass before building. WHAT ALREADY HELPS. Objectives carry a `period` (e.g. 'FY26 Q1') and a commitment limit; attribution is initiative-only, so an initiative maps to OKRs and its OKRs imply a period; the portfolio board already shows its own initiatives plus a band per linked team board, and each team board shows its initiatives by rollup; linkTeamInitiative creates a team initiative beneath a management one so it rolls up. OPEN QUESTIONS TO SETTLE FIRST. (1) Is 'this quarter's initiatives' derived — the initiatives attributed to that period's OKRs — or an explicit record/snapshot? The derived reading reuses existing data with no model change, so try it first. (2) Do initiatives need their own period field, or does the OKR period carry it? (3) How does a team 'take on' an initiative: create a new team initiative (linkTeamInitiative) or claim an existing one? (4) Is there a commit step (proposed vs committed for the quarter), or is the plan just the current state? (5) What must the department see at a glance: per-team lists, OKR coverage gaps (an OKR with no initiatives, an initiative serving no OKR), and capacity against the commitment limit. SUGGESTED SHAPE, reusing existing views. A period-scoped planning surface: pick the quarter, then show each team in the department with its initiatives for that quarter alongside the OKRs they serve, calling out gaps. Prefer a mode on the Objectives view or the portfolio board over a new top-level view, and reuse the board's Initiatives workflow for the per-team lists. OUT OF SCOPE until the design pass says otherwise: anything needing a new persisted entity (a plan/commitment record) — capture that as a follow-up rather than guessing now.
tasks.testStrategy: Walk the scenario end to end: pick a quarter and, for each team in the department, confirm a list of initiatives appears and each maps to at least one OKR; verify a gap (an OKR with no initiative, or an initiative serving no OKR) is surfaced; confirm a newly planned initiative shows up in that team's list and rolls up to the department. Unit-test any new derivation (e.g. 'initiatives for a period') and the gap detection. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Flight-level bands: an acyclic board-aggregation DAG with operational / coordination / strategic lenses
tasks.description: Model flight levels as bands (lenses) over one board-aggregation graph so large orgs can nest coordination boards at any depth, instead of a fixed three-tier level enum.
tasks.details: WHERE WE ARE. BoardLevel = 'portfolio' | 'project' | 'team', but every behavioural check is binary on 'portfolio' (BoardView routes level === 'portfolio' to ManagementBoard; BoardSettings shows 'Linked team boards' only for a portfolio; addBoard only initialises teamBoardIds for a portfolio). So 'project' is an inert label that renders as a team board, and the model can only express two tiers. Large orgs need Team -> Value stream -> Line of business -> ... -> Strategy, i.e. L2 can repeat. THE SHAPE. A board is either a work board (renders lanes/cards) or an aggregating board (renders its own outcomes plus a band per linked board). The band picks the LENS; depth is free. (1) Rename Board.teamBoardIds -> Board.linkedBoardIds (depth-agnostic; same migration). (2) Replace the level enum with a band: Board.band = 'operational' | 'coordination' | 'strategic'. (3) Aggregation is a DAG, not a tree: multiple parents already work because the link list lives on the aggregator, so a team can serve several value streams and a value stream can serve several lines of business; children may be MIXED (a coordination board can link teams AND other coordination boards). Enforce acyclicity: a board may link any board that is not already an ancestor of it (this replaces the current level-aware candidate filter in ManagementBoard/BoardSettings/ItemPanel). (4) Bands render type-agnostically - ManagementBoard already renders any linked board through BoardSummary without checking its level, so that part is nearly free. (5) Derive up the aggregation graph, not just the item tree: descendantBoards(boardId) (which teams roll up under a line of business - needed for the strategic demand-vs-capability lens) and aggregated cross-board dependencies (a line of business should see the handoffs its value streams carry). (6) Replace level === 'portfolio' with an aggregation predicate everywhere (BoardView routing, BoardSettings, addBoard, candidate lists). NAMING. The middle band is 'Coordination' (the lens); the board's NAME carries the domain word ('Payments value stream', 'Retail line of business'). The current Portfolio VIEW becomes the coordination surface; a new strategic lens is added at the top (see task 47 and 45). UI copy goes depth/type-agnostic: 'Linked boards' never 'Linked teams'; band headings derived from the children; LevelBadge labels Operational / Coordination / Strategic; BoardSettings type picker follows. MIGRATION. Persisted 'level': old 'portfolio' AND old 'project' both become the coordination band; the new strategic altitude starts empty. Note 'portfolio' is reused with a different meaning, so the mapping must be explicit. Bundle the teamBoardIds -> linkedBoardIds rename into the same version bump. Also update AGENTS.md (the current 'a board is either a management board (portfolio) or a team board' binary statement). SEED. A realistic N-deep demo (Team -> Value stream -> Line of business -> Strategy) that proves the recursion; today the seed has only L1 + L3. OUT OF SCOPE. The strategic lens's decision content (commitment, OKR coverage) - see task 47; and the quarterly-planning surface - see task 45.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test the aggregation predicate and acyclicity (a board cannot link an ancestor), descendantBoards over a 3-deep chain, and the migration (old 'portfolio'/'project' -> coordination, teamBoardIds -> linkedBoardIds). Over CDP: open a coordination board with mixed children and confirm a band per child; drill from a line of business into a value stream into a team. Confirm the seed's N-deep demo renders. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Strategic initiatives as first-class L3 items; OKRs attach at the top and inherit down
tasks.description: Strategic initiatives live on L3 portfolio boards as ordinary initiatives; OKRs attach only to them, and every other altitude connects up with the standard parent/child relationship.
tasks.details: THE DECISION. A 'strategic initiative' is just an Item of the Initiative type placed on a strategic-band board - no strategic flag, no Strategy entity. This makes L3 the top of the same pattern every other altitude already follows: a board owns its initiatives and the decomposition connects them. It reuses the three primitives already in the model: Placement (it lives on the L3 board), decomposition (it connects down), attribution (it carries the OKRs). ONE RELATION, TWO HOMES. OKRs attach ONLY to strategic initiatives. The L3 board is the initiative-first lens ('which OKRs does this strategic initiative serve?') and the Objectives view is the OKR-first lens ('which strategic initiatives serve this OKR?'); both edit the same attribution edges, so the OKR definition itself is not duplicated. Lower levels never learn a new mechanism: a value-stream initiative just sets its parent to a strategic initiative, and the lineage breadcrumb already renders the walk OKR -> strategic initiative -> ... -> card. Rollup is free (status stays derived from leaf work). GAPS ARE FIRST-CLASS. The L3 lens must surface a strategic initiative with no OKR and an OKR with no strategic initiative - that is the 'what is unowned / what not to do' signal, not a silent allowance. DECISIONS TO SETTLE. (1) One parent only: decomposition gives a value-stream initiative exactly one strategic parent, so 'serves two strategic initiatives' is not expressible - split the work, or later extend attribution to point at strategic initiatives. Keep one parent for now; the constraint does the disciplining. (2) OKRs at the top ONLY, or you lose the plan-vs-work distinction and coverage. (3) Does the L3 board also cap strategic initiatives per period, like the 3-5 OKR commitment limit? (4) OKRs carry the period and strategic initiatives inherit it; decide whether a strategic initiative may span quarters (allowed is probably right - the OKR period is the planning anchor, not a hard boundary). GUARD RAILS. No strategic/level field on items ('strategic' is where it sits, derived from its board and place in the tree); no new entity; status stays derived at every altitude. CROSS-REFS. Needs task 46 for the strategic band to exist at all; this is the model that makes task 45 (quarterly planning) precise: a quarter's plan is that period's OKRs -> their strategic initiatives -> the value-stream and team initiatives rolling up beneath them.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test that OKR attribution is refused below the strategic band (or that the L3 gap derivation reports unmapped strategic initiatives and unserved OKRs). Over CDP: create a strategic initiative on the L3 board, attach an OKR from the L3 lens, then attach a value-stream initiative as its child and confirm the lineage breadcrumb on a leaf card walks up to the OKR. Confirm an initiative with no OKR and an OKR with no initiative are both surfaced. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Board workspace: browse, search and open boards
tasks.description: A top-level Boards workspace listing every board in the organisation, grouped by band, with search. Rows carry the name and band only; opening one switches to that board. Reachable from a TopBar toggle and from the board picker.
tasks.details: A new top-level view toggled from the TopBar beside Objectives / Archive (showBoards), and reachable from a 'Manage boards…' footer entry in the board picker so the switcher is not a dead end. The list groups by band (Portfolio → Program → Team) then name, and each board appears exactly ONCE: the aggregation graph is a DAG — a team board can be linked by two programs — so nesting under a parent would either duplicate rows or pick one and lie. The board picker reached the same conclusion. A row carries only the band badge and the name for now. A search field filters by name. Selecting a row calls selectBoard(id) and leaves the workspace. Archived boards are hidden (task 50). Each row also offers Delete, routed through the existing confirm dialog and removeBoard. Board admin also stays inside each board — the workspace is another way in, not the only one.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test the grouping/ordering and the name filter. Over CDP: open the workspace from the TopBar and from the picker footer; confirm every board appears exactly once, grouped by band, and that search narrows the list; open a board and confirm the app switches to it; delete a board and confirm the modal appears and the board leaves both the list and the picker. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Board workspace: create a board
tasks.description: Create a board from the workspace: a name plus a band, optionally from a template.
tasks.details: A 'New board' control in the workspace header collecting a name and a band (team / program / portfolio). addBoard currently defaults to team, so it needs to take an explicit band and seed linkedBoardIds for non-team bands, as the store already does when a band is passed. The template choice arrives with task 51 — until then the standard four typed columns are the only starting point, which is today's behaviour. The existing TopBar edit-mode create stays: the workspace is another way in, not the only one.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test addBoard with an explicit band, including that a non-team board starts with an empty linkedBoardIds and that the board gets the standard typed columns. Over CDP: create a board from the workspace for each band, confirm it appears under the right group in the list and can be opened. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Archive boards (retire a board without destroying it)
tasks.description: Let a board be archived: hidden from the picker, the workspace's default list and the aggregation bands, but not destroyed. Mirrors item archiving (task 12).
tasks.details: Add Board.archived (with archivedAt) plus archiveBoard / unarchiveBoard. An archived board is hidden from the board picker, the workspace's default list and the aggregation bands — a retired program must stop collecting rollups — and can be revealed with an 'include archived' toggle in the workspace. It stays openable by deep link (?board=…), and its lanes, items, placements and edges are untouched; nothing is deleted. Persist version bump + migrate. SETTLED, and built: (a) archived boards KEEP their aggregation edges. Archiving never mutates config, exactly as item archiving never removes an item from the hierarchy; the board is filtered out of the picker, the workspace's list, the aggregation bands and the link candidates (activeBoards in the domain), so the graph reads cleanly and unarchiving restores it with nothing to repair. (b) An archived board is FULLY USABLE when opened — archiving is about visibility, not immutability, and archived items behave the same way. Opening one shows an archived chip with a Restore action on both board surfaces, so it is never a surprise.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test archive/unarchive; that archived boards are filtered out of the picker, the workspace list and the aggregation bands; and that the migration leaves older persisted state working. Over CDP: archive a board and confirm it leaves the picker and the workspace, and disappears as a band from the board that aggregated it; open it by deep link; toggle 'include archived' and unarchive; confirm its bands return. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Board templates: define, save and instantiate
tasks.description: A template is a board design, not its work: save a board's design as a template, and create new boards from it.
tasks.details: Add BoardTemplate { id, name, band, lanes, cardTypeIds?, defaultCardTypeId?, wipEnforcement? } as a new persisted collection (persist version bump + migrate). lanes is the board's lane tree — names, orientation, stage and wipLimit — with fresh ids minted on instantiation. A template carries NO items, placements or linked boards: those are org-specific. 'Save as template' from a board; 'New board' then offers the built-in standard (the four typed columns) plus saved templates. SETTLE: how much of Board settings a template carries (is lanes + card types + WIP enough?), and whether 'save as template' is offered from Board settings as well as the workspace. Note: this is the templates half of task 21, which should be re-pointed at the wizard and duplicate board so the two do not drift.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test instantiate: a board created from a template has the template's lane structure with fresh unique ids, the same stages and WIP limits, and no placements or linked boards, and the template itself is unchanged. Round-trip a template through persistence. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Board templates: manage the library
tasks.description: List, rename and remove templates from the workspace.
tasks.details: A templates section in the workspace (or a small dialog) listing saved templates with their band and lane count, allowing rename and removal behind the confirm dialog. Removing a template must not affect boards already created from it.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit-test template CRUD (add/rename/remove, unique ids). Over CDP: rename a template and confirm it survives a reload; remove one and confirm boards created from it are untouched. Run npm test.

tasks.title: Board workspace: per-board headline, graph gaps, and board admin
tasks.description: Deferred from the workspace's first slice: a richer per-board summary, inline graph gaps, and board admin from the workspace.
tasks.details: (a) A per-board headline beyond name + band — the initiative count, or a stage spread from rollupOf().bucket (cheap), or a single rolled-up percentage, which needs defining (across the board's own initiatives, or across all work beneath it) and means computing rollups for every board at once — settle the cost first. (b) Inline graph gaps, matching the app's habit of surfacing gaps (okrCoverage, uncommittedBelow): a board with no initiatives; a program or portfolio with nothing linked; a team board no coordination board links. (c) Rename / change band, and link / unlink aggregation edges, from the workspace. Board admin still stays inside each board — this adds a second way in, it does not move it.
tasks.testStrategy: Manual verification per item, plus unit tests for any new derivation (the board headline and the gap detection). Run npm test.
